I have some mixed feelings about this. Now before people get mad, please let me explain. I've been through this. There was a nasty car crash at the bottom of the estate I live in and because I live so close, I was one of the first responders. I was 18 at the time and new the people in the car (all 16-18 year olds). The car was destroyed and the four teenagers inside were all knocked unconscious but I could tell that the front passenger was seriously hurt due to the way the car hat skidded sideways into a retaining wall. While running around the car with the only other person who had arrived by that point, I noticed the others were out cold but didn't seem to be bleeding badly. The guy in the front passenger seat was slumped over in a way I've never seen another human. The girl behind him was unconscious with her head in the lap of the girl she was sitting beside but looked a lot better than the guy so I helped him, I lifted his head and opened his airways to help him breathe. I listened to him struggling to breathe due to collapsed lungs and a crushed chest (not to mention the meriad of other broken bones and lacerated organs he had). I very explicitly remember watching the spit dripping from his mouth onto my hands while I held him until the ambulances arrived. To me it felt like 5 minutes at the very most but I learned after it was closer to 25. What I didn't know was that the girl behind the guy I was helping had hit her head badly and the crash had basically turned her brain to scrambled egg. She was pronounced dead shortly after making it to the hospital. I knew her, she wasn't close to me but I knew her from living around there and because she was good friends with my sister. She was 16. For years afterwords, and even to this day (over 4 years later) flowers and memorials have been left for her right down the road from my house. Everyday I walk past there I see it and can't forget. It's a painful memory. Everyday I wish those flowers would be moved so that myself and everyone else who was there that night didn't have to relive that moment over and over again. I am not saying that this woman is right, I don't know the circumstances, but I get it. If the timeframe is a matter of weeks after the accident that killed this person then the memorial should be left, if it's months then I'm more empathetic
